items.headline: Nifty gains 0.46% on the week to 25,144, a third straight weekly rise; smallcaps add 3.15%
items.summary: Bank stocks outperformed with a 3.7% weekly gain; the midcap index rose 1.56%. Friday's 0.61% fall trimmed the advance. Analysts see support at 24,800 and resistance at 25,400–25,500. Rally slowing after last week's 8.6% jump.
items.rationale: Momentum is fading as inflation and oil return as worries; broader-market strength shows domestic risk appetite is intact but the index needs fresh inflows to clear resistance.

items.headline: Foreign investors buy about ₹33,340 crore of Indian shares in the week, extending November inflows
items.summary: Exchange-based weekly tallies vary by source, but all show heavy buying for a second week after October's ₹34,843 crore outflow. Analysts warn that slower inflows with continued domestic fund selling could raise volatility. Ongoing.
items.rationale: Foreign buying has driven the rally and supported the rupee; its persistence despite higher US yields is the main cushion for equities.

items.headline: Brent settles at $95.84, down about 2.5% on the week, as the IEA sees a supply surplus this quarter
items.summary: Friday's move was 2 cents; WTI settled near $88.56. The IEA said the market will be in surplus for the first time since the war began, with Gulf exports at 18.4 million barrels a day in October. Second weekly fall.
items.rationale: A surplus outlook caps crude even with Hormuz risk, limiting further damage to India's import bill and inflation; prices remain well above pre-war levels.

items.headline: Iran now says three oil tankers caught fire after striking mines in Hormuz; US says routes are clear
items.summary: The claim adds a third ship to Friday's reports; none has been publicly identified and Hormuz traffic stays far below pre-war levels. Talks remain stalled, with Iran awaiting a US reply to seven conditions. Escalating.
items.rationale: Mine claims, verified or not, raise war-risk premiums and deter transits on the route for most of India's Gulf crude and LNG.

items.headline: India-US trade deal in final stage with the bulk of issues sorted, foreign minister says
items.summary: He said remaining concerns are mostly on the American side. The commerce minister has said the first tranche is finalised and in legal drafting, to take effect once India's tariff edge over rivals is assured. Progressing from Friday.
items.rationale: A signed first tranche would lock in lower US tariffs than competitors face, helping textiles, engineering goods and pharma exporters and supporting foreign-investor sentiment.

items.headline: Rabi sowing at 178.25 lakh hectares by 13 November, 11.34% behind last year; wheat down 15.28%
items.summary: Wheat covers 50.07 lakh hectares, pulses 47 lakh (down 14.34%) and mustard 59.31 lakh (down 8.45%). The gap has narrowed from 17.21% a week earlier and 46% on 30 October. Easing but still behind.
items.rationale: Lagging winter sowing threatens wheat, pulses and oilseed output just as food inflation runs near 9%, though the shortfall is closing as planting catches up.

items.headline: October wholesale inflation due Monday; forecasts point above 12% after September's 11.39% series high
items.summary: Consensus is about 12.1%, with some forecasts at 12.35%. It follows retail inflation of 6.09% on Thursday. Escalating: wholesale inflation was 9.92% in August.
items.rationale: A double-digit wholesale print signals input-cost pressure still feeding into retail prices, squeezing manufacturers' margins and reinforcing rate-hike expectations.

items.headline: UN urges the US and Iran to let fertiliser shipments through the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: The appeal comes as rabi sowing lags and days after India raised its winter fertiliser subsidy 64% to ₹62,370 crore on higher global prices. New.
items.rationale: Gulf suppliers ship much of India's urea, ammonia and LNG feedstock; blocked cargoes raise prices and the subsidy bill during the sowing season.

items.headline: Foreign minister calls China border 'more alive' and says India needs more troops there long term
items.summary: A separate report says a Chinese military aircraft entered Indian airspace over Sikkim for 20 minutes. New tension alongside a planned visit by a Pakistani minister for regional talks.
items.rationale: Higher border spending supports defence and infrastructure orders but adds to fiscal demands; any flare-up would hurt risk appetite.
